findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:346-348 (matcher-value-empty) tags an EMPTY literal-line value as R1-3. R1-3s own enumerated list (spec:499-504) explicitly names only value longer than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace for value-bound failures — it never mentions empty/too-short. The codebase itself already applies this exact reasoning to the two sibling clauses of the same rule-1 triple: trimmed -> R1-3 (explicitly named in R1-3s list) and blocklisted -> R1-2 (explicitly named in R1-2s list, per envelope.ts:393-400). non-empty is the third clause and is NOT named in R1-3s list, so by the codes own established methodology it should route to R1-2 like blocklisted, not R1-3 like trimmed. Failing input: matchers:[{id:L1,kind:literal-line,value:"",stream:combined,polarity:present-in-red}] -> current output tags matcher-value-empty as R1-3; expected R1-2 per §1.3 rule 1. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:274-434: the matcherSetEvaluable gate (line 385, requiring rawMatchers.length in [1,maxMatchers] AND bounded.length>0) suppresses the ENTIRE §1.3 block — per-matcher rule1/2 AND the rule-3 class-only-present-in-red check — whenever the matcher COUNT is out of bounds. The DEV handoff's phrase 'no process spawning' was too absolute and is not a code defect. What must be fixed is the EVIDENCE: either narrow the claim to what the snapshot proves (no writes under .lattice, no chain record, no gate change) or genuinely assert the spawn set. Do not remove the git read.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed - see B-9ff1:F-002. findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs:126-141 and packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:386-398: the committed read-only proof snapshots per-file SHA-256 hashes of the .lattice tree before/after invoking red_evidence_envelope_check, plus static registry-flag assertions (ownershipClass readOnly, READ_ONLY_COMMANDS membership). Neither technique can detect an errant child-process spawn that writes nothing under .lattice (e.g. outside the repo, to a temp dir, or a network call) — a directory hash and a static classification flag are not behavioral evidence against process spawning. This is a test-assurance gap, not a functional defect: direct source reading confirms the only child processes in the call path are the two read-only git commands (rev-parse/show) inside readCommittedTargetBindings (packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/target-bindings.ts:141,172,180), and the handlers own docstring (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts:347-355) correctly and narrowly claims spawns no RED run rather than an absolute spawns nothing claim. Flagging per the review brief item 4 (a test that only hashes a directory cannot detect a process spawn) so the gap between what is claimed and what the regression can actually detect is on record; no code change is indicated, only stronger test assurance (e.g. intercepting child_process.spawn/spawnSync during the check() calls and asserting only git rev-parse/show occur) would close it.

findings.desc: Empirical read-only check (post-merge, unaffected by the merge — cli-engine.ts and stale-detector.ts have 0 commits in d47a35787d..HEAD): running node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_envelope_check against B-9ff1 (which is genuinely stale in REVIEW) DID append a row to .lattice/activity.jsonl, contradicting the literal comment at packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts:23-25 ('It must append NOTHING (no hook, no activity log, no process event)'). Root cause: cli-engine.ts writeLog is gated by 'shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0' (line 1416/1488) — the staleWarnings OR-clause bypasses the READ_ONLY_COMMANDS suppression for EVERY read-only command (not specific to red_evidence_envelope_check), by design, for stale-state trend analysis, and is self-limited by a cooldown (suppressRecentlyEmittedWarnings in stale-detector.ts) so it fires at most once per cooldown window. Verified: a second story_get call immediately after (same stale story) did NOT re-append, confirming the cooldown, not red_evidence_envelope_check-specific misbehavior. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this predates B-9ff1 entirely (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts and core/stale-detector.ts are untouched in the whole d47a35787d..HEAD range, so it already existed when RP-003 passed pre-merge) and is shared uniformly by all ~90 READ_ONLY_COMMANDS members, not introduced or worsened by this story or by the merge. The formal guarantee the story actually makes in command-policy.ts (line 445: executes no envelope, writes no artifact/process event/chain record, and changes no gate verdict) remains TRUE and verified — activity.jsonl is generic CLI session telemetry, not one of those four enumerated categories, and no gate/verdict/artifact/chain state is touched. Recommend softening the activity-policy.ts comment's absolute no-activity-log wording rather than any functional change. Repro: cd worktree; run node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_envelope_check --storyId=B-9ff1 --assertionFile=<any path> --json while the story is stale, and diff a full .lattice/ shasum snapshot before/after — activity.jsonl hash changes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b63dcad96b86de010dfc3be10e48e14016cb2428 (comment-only, one file, 11 insertions / 3 deletions in packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts). The finding is REAL and was independently reproduced by the main agent rather than accepted on the reviewer's word: grep -c red_evidence_envelope_check .lattice/activity.jsonl returns 20, so the command has in fact appended activity rows. Root cause: the writeLog call sites in cli-engine.ts read shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0, and the right-hand disjunct is an independent path that bypasses READ_ONLY_COMMANDS suppression for ANY command, read-only included, whenever the story carries an uncooled stale warning (STALE_WARNING_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 minutes, core/stale-detector.ts). shouldWriteActivityLog itself is correct and does return false for members. What was defective was this story's OWN comment, added by GREEN commit e88bb78a65, which asserted the command must append NOTHING including no activity log and that membership guarantees exactly that. Membership is necessary but not sufficient, so the assertion was false as written, and it was the only absolute claim of its kind in that file. The comment now states what membership actually guarantees, names the stale-warning bypass and its cooldown by file and symbol rather than by line number, and records that the formal contract in core/command-policy.ts (writes no artifact, no process event, no chain record, changes no gate verdict) holds unconditionally because activity.jsonl is generic CLI session telemetry outside those four categories. Marked partially_mitigated rather than fixed because the underlying cli-engine bypass is deliberately NOT repaired here: making the stale-warning path respect READ_ONLY_COMMANDS would change shared behaviour for roughly ninety commands and is out of this story's scope; that systemic defect is filed as separate follow-up work. findings.desc: activity-policy.ts:23-33 (the F-014 repair, commit b63dcad96b) states as an unconditional fact that 'Membership here makes shouldWriteActivityLog (this file) return false' for red_evidence_envelope_check. That is only true when process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY !== '1' — shouldWriteActivityLog (same file, lines 151-159) returns, for any read-only command, exactly `process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY === '1'`, i.e. false by default but TRUE when that var is set. LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1 is not an obscure test knob: it is this repo's own documented 'global-fallback' Codex entrypoint env (init-assets.ts:148-163 LATTICE_CODEX_ADAPTER_MANIFEST.recommendedEntrypoints, init-assets.ts:213-238 CODEX_README template, core/codex-adapter-checks.ts:57/502/607 GLOBAL_CODEX_FALLBACK_COMMAND), recommended precisely when a Codex session lacks the local wrapper. Under that real, documented, in-repo operating mode, red_evidence_envelope_check membership in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS does NOT make shouldWriteActivityLog return false — it makes it return true, and every invocation appends an activity.jsonl row. This is the same class of overclaim (a classification-driven guarantee stated as unconditional when a real code path flips it) that this very comment was rewritten this round to stop making about the staleWarnings bypass — the new text names that bypass explicitly but omits this second, equally real one on the very sentence introducing the primary claim.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit ee73b9f66df8ac0ba91b81ef2ab8a455287f3735. The F-014 repair comment in packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts named only the stale-warning bypass and still asserted unconditionally that membership makes shouldWriteActivityLog return false. It now states that membership settles two surfaces outright (hooks and process events, both gated on isReadOnlyCommand alone) and explicitly does NOT settle the activity log, then names BOTH bypasses. This finding and F-020 are the same defect found independently by two lanes. The underlying fact, verified independently by the main agent and not taken on the reviewer's word: membership in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS is necessary but NOT sufficient to suppress an activity-log row. Two independent bypasses exist. (1) shouldWriteActivityLog returns process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY === '1' for read-only commands, and that variable is not a test knob: it is baked into GLOBAL_CODEX_FALLBACK_COMMAND in core/codex-adapter-checks.ts and into the generated Codex wrapper in src/init-assets.ts. (2) Both writeLog call sites in cli-engine.ts read shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0, and the right disjunct appends one generic session row for ANY command while the story carries an uncooled stale warning (STALE_WARNING_COOLDOWN_MS, 30 minutes, core/stale-detector.ts). Empirically .lattice/activity.jsonl held 20 rows for this command when the defect was found and 28 by the time it was repaired. What remains unconditionally true is the core/command-policy.ts contract: no artifact, no process event, no chain record, and no gate verdict change. The hook and process-event suppressions are also genuinely unconditional, because both are gated on isReadOnlyCommand alone with no second term - those clauses were kept, not weakened. Deliberately NOT repaired here: the shared cli-engine bypass itself. Making the stale-warning path respect READ_ONLY_COMMANDS would change behaviour for roughly ninety commands and is filed as separate follow-up work. Also left alone as sibling-story material: the six 'Nothing written.' refusal strings belonging to the W2b/W2c mutating chain commands, and the F-028 usage_sweep comment from story B-70e9 - both filed separately. Verification after the change: build clean, npx tsc --noEmit clean, red-evidence-envelope-smoke OK, and all five packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-*.mjs pass. A second commit 63a9092d7fbfe41b15a3f825f231333e91a3782f widened the repair beyond the reviewers' file list after the implementer reported three more instances of the same absolute for this same command, one of them user-facing: the catalog description in cli/command-catalog.ts surfaced through help, the phase-bucket comment in core/config.ts, and the registration comment in registry.ts. Leaving a user-visible 'writes nothing' in the catalog while fixing the printed strings would have been inconsistent.
